questions.q: What does it mean that Microsoft Fabric is a SaaS platform, compared to Databricks' compute model?
options: You never choose a VM size, runtime version, or autoscaling bounds — every engine runs against a managed capacity instead
It means Fabric has no compute at all, only storage
It means Fabric only runs on-premises, never in the cloud
It means Fabric requires manually configuring a Spark cluster before use
questions.explain: This is a real, structural difference from Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 4's compute-creation form.

questions.q: What is OneLake, at a high level?
options: One logical data lake for the entire organization, shared by every Fabric engine — Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Eventhouse alike
A separate storage account each Fabric item must configure independently
A synonym for a single Delta table
A feature exclusive to Fabric's real-time analytics engine only
questions.explain: This plays a similar unifying role to Unity Catalog's metastore, one governance layer across workspaces.

questions.q: How does Fabric relate to Delta Lake, the format covered in the previous course?
options: Fabric standardizes on Delta Lake as its shared table format too — that earlier material is directly reusable knowledge here
Fabric uses a completely different, incompatible table format
Fabric only supports plain Parquet, never Delta
Delta Lake only works within Databricks, never within Fabric
questions.explain: This is why the previous course's Delta Lake chapter transfers directly into this one.
